marie: quick sync — i ran a fast-fallback prototype on draft-14b-quant (4bit PTQ) under bursty traffic to validate p50/p99 and a small eval sweep. high-level: latency wins, small code-quality regressions observed. attaching short notes below.
sam: numbers?
ravi: short paste from the run: `baseline (fp16): p50=65ms p99=610ms`, `fast-fallback (4bit+fast-fallback): p50=52ms p99=420ms`. cost estimate about -23% GPU token cost at our load.
sam: nice. where's the quality hit?
marie: mostly on code-generation correctness tests. on our 2k holdout (60% code, 40% convs) exact-match for code unit tests dropped ~4pts; ROUGE-L on convs basically unchanged. not catastrophic but noticeable.
leo: what triggers the fallback? queue depth / latency threshold? any changes to sampling?
marie: fallback policy used: if queue_depth > 12 OR observed tail_latency > 200ms then route to fast-path (aggressive KV-prefetch + quant-compact kernels). sampling untouched (top-p=0.95).
ravi: repro note + command we used:
```
# run benchmark
./tools/run_infer_burst.sh --model draft-14b-quant --fallback-policy "qd>12||p99>200" --seed 42 --batch-policy instant
```
also logged token-level traces; noticed more early-token divergence for code prompts (first 8 tokens often differ).
sam: did you isolate whether it's quantization vs the fast-path scheduling?
marie: good call — we ran two ablations: (A) quantized model on baseline runtime, (B) quantized + fast-fallback. A had ~1.2pt drop; B had ~4pt drop. so scheduling/kv-prefetch behavior seems to amplify small quant errors for deterministic code gen.
leo: can we mitigate without full rollback? ideas: (1) conservative fallback for code route, (2) hybrid: for prompts flagged as "code-like" keep fp16 until stable, (3) micro-batching tweaks to reduce divergence.
ravi: i can try conservative thresholds: raise queue_depth to 18 and p99 to 300ms for code cohort, and keep existing aggressive policy for convs. also try increasing KV warmup for first token.
marie: propose quick A/B: 5k prompts, stratified by code/convo, run traffic weighted canary (10%) for 24h, monitor exact-match, p99, and regression alarms (>=2pt drop triggers rollback).
deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated for eng-ml/canary/draft-14b-quant at 2026-03-21T15:10:00Z :rocket:
marie: perfect — ravi please push conservative thresholds and include a small eval harness that records first-8-token divergence rate.
ravi: on it, will post logs here when done.
sam: also add human spot-check on 50 failing code samples — the diffs give intuition about severity.
marie: agreed. if the errors are benign formatting vs semantic, we can keep and iterate; if failing tests, rollback. thanks all :thumbsup:
